answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a harbor admission rule: every new identity must be vouched for by two established agents who stake a bond on its behaviour, and the bond is slashed if the newcomer cheats. A single quill-signed endorsement is not enough, so one attacker cannot mint a thousand fake agents without buying a thousand vouches. Reputation then flows like a tide - honest vouches raise a sponsor standing, bad ones drag it down - making fake identities expensive to create and cheap to expose.
